reasons: Logic is clear and duplicate handling is present.
Re-adding a contact clears its tags.
Corrupt data can be overwritten silently.

terms.meaning: browser storage that keeps data across page refreshes
a short text label that identifies an application in web addresses and lookups

sections.name: File setup, ContactRole
sections.title: Purpose and role labels
sections.what: States that the store holds contacts from search or manual entry, saved in the browser, and defines the allowed role labels.
sections.why: Explains the design and the role categories.

sections.name: Contact
sections.title: Contact record shape
sections.what: The fields for one contact: name, title, company, role, links, email, source, notes, tags, dates and linked applications.
sections.why: Gives every contact the same structure.
sections.watch_out: The source value rocketreach is listed, but nothing in this file creates it.

sections.name: load
sections.title: Loading contacts
sections.what: Reads saved contacts from browser storage, returning an empty list when nothing is saved or the data is broken.
sections.watch_out: Broken data is treated as empty, so the next save overwrites it.

sections.name: save
sections.title: Saving contacts
sections.what: Writes the full contact list to browser storage and notifies the page that contacts changed.
sections.why: Keeps the screen up to date after edits.
sections.watch_out: Every change rewrites the whole list.

sections.name: getContacts
sections.title: Getting all contacts
sections.why: Newest contacts are the most relevant to the user.
sections.watch_out: Sorting relies on the creation dates being text in the same format.

sections.name: getContactsByCompany
sections.title: Contacts for a company
sections.what: Returns contacts whose company name loosely matches the given company.
sections.why: Companies are written in many ways, so the match is loose.
sections.watch_out: A contact with an empty company name matches every company.

sections.name: getContactsByApplication
sections.title: Contacts for an application
sections.what: Returns contacts linked to one application by its slug.
sections.why: Shows who is connected to a given job.
sections.watch_out: The match depends on the slug being exactly the same.

sections.name: searchContacts
sections.title: Searching contacts
sections.what: Finds contacts whose name, company, title, email or tags contain the search text, ignoring case.
sections.why: Gives the user a quick lookup on the contacts screen.
sections.watch_out: An empty search returns everything, unsorted.

sections.name: addContact
sections.title: Adding a contact
sections.what: Adds a new contact, or updates an existing one that has the same LinkedIn link, email, or name and company.
sections.why: Avoids duplicate entries from repeated searches.
sections.watch_out: When a contact is updated, its tags are replaced with an empty list unless new tags are given, which erases earlier tags.

sections.name: updateContact
sections.title: Updating a contact
sections.what: Changes some fields of one contact found by its ID and leaves the other fields as they were.
sections.why: Lets small edits happen without rewriting the whole record.
sections.watch_out: Does nothing and reports no error if the ID is not found.

sections.name: deleteContact
sections.title: Deleting a contact
sections.what: Removes one contact by its ID.
sections.why: Lets the user clean up the list.
sections.watch_out: Deletion is permanent and there is no undo in this file.

sections.name: markContacted
sections.title: Marking a contact as contacted
sections.what: Records the current time as the last contact date for one person.
sections.watch_out: It only records the time; it does not send anything.

sections.name: attachContactToApplication
sections.title: Linking a contact to an application
sections.what: Adds an application slug to a contact so the contact shows under that application.
sections.why: Connects people with the jobs they relate to.
sections.watch_out: Does nothing and reports no error if the contact ID is not found.

summary: Keeps the user's list of people to contact about jobs in browser storage, and handles adding, editing, searching, deleting and linking them to applications.
purpose: Lets the user track hiring managers, referral candidates, recruiters and other contacts.
why: The header states the contacts are saved per user in browser storage, so no server is needed.
how: 1. Loads the list from browser storage. 2. Adds a contact, or merges it into an existing one if the LinkedIn link, email, or name and company match. 3. Updates, deletes or marks contacts. 4. Searches or filters by company, application or text. 5. Saves the list and notifies the page.
inputs: Contact details from search results or manual entry, contact IDs, application slugs, and search text.
outputs: Lists of contacts, or a contact record, and changes saved to browser storage.
risks: Names, emails and phone numbers are stored unencrypted in the browser. Re-adding a contact without tags replaces its existing tags with an empty list. Clearing browser data erases all contacts. Corrupt stored data is treated as empty and overwritten on the next save.
debug: Look at the browser local storage entry careeros_contacts. If the list looks empty, check that the stored data is valid JSON.
